governingStandard.phrase: EV-2 and EV-3 are not collapsed
attestedAt: harness.DR-G23.provider-well-formed-admission.preview.v2 (f48ba637…, the current occupancy per D-223, pinned by the subject itself) namedCorpusClasses[1].exactByteIntent — 'EV-2 and EV-3 are not collapsed.'
same artifact retainedEvidence[1].exactByteIntent — 'This member does not include unknown-to-covered conversion; that is EV-3.'
same artifact retainedEvidence[2].exactByteIntent — 'This member is not collapsed into EV-2.'
provider-only-output-contract.v3 negativeTests.NT-5.input — 'A Coverage payload that narrows, widens, or converts unknown to covered relative to the host-requested domain.' Three disjuncts, not one.
g23-input-corpus.v1 names narrows, widens and unknown-to-covered as three separate initial states.
governingStandard.why: G23 exists to prove the host refuses each Coverage-domain mutation mode. A retained refusal only discharges the class it can be attributed to. If one fixture instantiates two mutation modes at once, observing a refusal proves the host caught something, not that it caught narrowing — and the occupancy the subject pins as current forbids exactly that collapse by name, in both directions.
governingStandard.whatTheCorpusGotRight: This is a large and genuine advance on the rejected v1, and most of it survives adversarial measurement. The NT-3 fixture is byte-identical to the pinned fact-plane.v1 vector fact-id-v1-typescript-declares at every one of its 14 fields except the single intended relationSchemaId mutation — key order included — and its anchor path src/a.ts is an exact member of that vector's context.snapshotFiles, which the catalog reproduces field-for-field. Claude M1 and Codex M1 are fully landed: zero Sha256Text form violations remain anywhere in the four fixtures, and contentSha256 correctly carries bare DigestHex per the closed definition rather than being over-corrected. Claude M2 and Codex M4 are fully landed and independently verified: all three coverageCommitments recompute exactly under deterministic CBOR, which is a much stronger result than a declared construction. Claude M4 and Codex M3 are fully landed: every coverage key draws relation/resolution from the live relationResolutionById map (imports/resolved-target, types/checked) and file and package are gone. Claude M5 is fully landed and is the sharpest single fix in the artifact — the widens fixture orders types/checked before imports/resolved-target, which is wrong under plain string comparison and right under canonical CBOR, so the ordering claim is discriminating rather than decorative. Claude M3 and S1 and S2 are landed. hostRequestedDomain really is the closed three-field RequestedCoverageDomainV1: the subject correctly drops the vector's non-schema expectedKeyCount and adds vectorConstants.subjectScope, and the copied domainCommitment then recomputes exactly over that assembled object, which proves the added subjectScope is the right one rather than an assertion. S4 is landed — leftoverDesignClosedIfAcceptedAndRecorded is empty and OBL-G23-FX-AUTHORING stays open. The finding-mapping table is complete and correct: all nine Claude ids and all five Codex ids are accounted for exactly once.

findings.title: The EV-2 narrows fixture also converts unknown to covered, collapsing EV-2 into EV-3 against the governing occupancy's explicit non-collapse requirement
findings.live: The subject pins its narrows domain to delivery.v2 wireSchema.coverageDomain.vectors[cross-universe-unavailable-two-targets] — named explicitly at pinnedHostContext.importsDomainVector, and confirmed by recomputation: the member's domainCommitment sha256:ad85230a… reproduces exactly over that vector's two keys plus vectorConstants.subjectScope. That same vector pins the host-side coverage expectation for this exact domain: expectedCoverage is two entries, BOTH coverageState 'unknown' with deficiency 'provider-unavailable', under terminal frameType Unavailable / snapshot-resolution-input-missing. The current occupancy harness.DR-G23.provider-well-formed-admission.preview.v2 — which the subject pins at f48ba637… and quotes as exactByteIntent — states at retainedEvidence[1] 'This member does not include unknown-to-covered conversion; that is EV-3', at retainedEvidence[2] 'This member is not collapsed into EV-2', and at namedCorpusClasses[1] 'EV-2 and EV-3 are not collapsed.'
findings.authored: The narrows fixture carries a single CoverageResultV1 whose coverageState is 'complete' and whose deficiency is null. Relative to the pinned domain the subject itself cites, the surviving key has moved from unknown/provider-unavailable to complete/null. That is the unknown-to-covered conversion, present inside the EV-2 member. No hostRequestedCoverageBaseline is declared for this member, nor for the widens member — the sibling EV-3 member is the only one of the three that declares one.
findings.whyItMatters: The subject is caught on both horns of the ambiguity it leaves open. If the baseline for this member is the pinned vector's expectedCoverage — the only coverage state pinned anywhere for this domain, and the domain the subject deliberately selected because it is the only pinned two-key domain — then the fixture carries a second, undeclared mutation of exactly the class the occupancy forbids mixing in, and the member's own mutation text ('CoverageV1.entries contain only the CBOR-first of the two pinned imports keys. The second imports key is missing.') is an incomplete description of the authored bytes. If instead no baseline governs this member, then the mutation is unfalsifiable: nothing in the pinned record establishes what the unmutated payload would have been, which is the precise defect Codex G23FXV1-M5 raised as 'does not retain an exact unknown baseline' and Claude S3 raised as 'EV-2 and EV-3 are separated only by an under-determined prose baseline'. Both are recorded in appliesFindingsOf as ACCEPTED and landed. On either horn they are landed for EV-3 only, so those two dispositions over-claim. This is not a hypothetical: the subject demonstrably knows the remedy, because it applied it to EV-3 and to nothing else.
findings.failureScenario: G23 executes the EV-2 narrows member. The host refuses the payload and the record is retained as EV-2 evidence. The refusal is unattributable — the host may have refused the missing second key, or the complete/null claim over a domain whose pinned coverage is unknown, and the retained bytes cannot distinguish them. EV-3's separate record then proves nothing EV-2 did not already contain, so the two members stop being independent evidence and the occupancy's non-collapse requirement is unmet by the very corpus authored to satisfy it. A later leftover-join remasurement measuring OBL-G23-FX-AUTHORING against these bytes would be measuring a corpus that cannot discharge EV-2.
findings.remedy: Add hostRequestedCoverageBaseline to the narrows member as two full CoverageResultV1 entries carrying the pinned vector's expectation — both imports keys at coverageState 'unknown', deficiency 'provider-unavailable', entryOrdinal 0 and 1 in canonical-CBOR key order — and re-author G23.nt5.coverage-narrows.json so its single surviving CBOR-first key stays coverageState 'unknown' with deficiency 'provider-unavailable'. Cardinality then becomes the only mutation and the narrowing is attributable on its own. Recompute that fixture's coverageCommitment over the new entries and update its digest in authoredCatalog.members[1].sha256 and in recordedInputs. Extend the member's mutation text to state the baseline it is measured against. Declare the same explicit baseline for the widens member, which today also retains none — benign in effect, since both its entries share one state and so introduce no conversion, but the same discipline gap. Then narrow the appliesFindingsOf dispositions for S3 and G23FXV1-M5 to what is actually landed, or re-land them across all three Coverage members.

findings.title: pinnedHostContext.coverageVectorConstants names a JSON path that does not exist in the digest-pinned delivery.v2
findings.live: delivery.v2 at the pinned digest 47b6cfd17338fafd407c554afe1951ab23d2896aac99bcfd272fc0894e3cabf3 carries vectorConstants at $.typescriptSemanticSubstrate.providerProtocol.wireSchema.coverageDomain.vectorConstants. There is no providerProtocol.coverageDomain node in those bytes; resolution fails at the third segment. Every other artifact in the repository that cites this node spells it with wireSchema — corpus-float-admission-sweep.v1 twice, and div2-subject-leaf-privacy.decision-brief.v1 twice. The subject is the only occurrence that omits the segment.
findings.whyItMatters: The corpus's authorityClaim rests on the sentence 'Host context is copied from pinned delivery.v2 coverageDomain vectors', and pinnedHostContext is the single block that says where those vectors live. A digest-pinned citation whose selector does not resolve in the pinned bytes is a custody defect in a document whose entire function is exact pinning — the same class of defect the register treats as a re-open condition elsewhere. The values themselves are correct: I resolved the real node and recomputed subjectScopeCommitment and both domainCommitments from it, and all three match the subject exactly, so this is a pointer defect and not a data defect. That is why it is SHOULD-FIX and not MUST-FIX. The sibling pointer pinnedHostContext.factCandidateVector resolves correctly.
findings.failureScenario: A later executor or reviewer resolves the pinned pointer against 47b6cfd1… to confirm the copied host context, gets nothing at the named path, and must either guess the intended node or record an unresolvable-selector conflict against an artifact whose data is in fact sound.

observationsNotFindings: The four authoredCatalog member ids match g23-input-corpus.v1 initialStates ids exactly and in order, and every inputCorpusId round-trips. The input corpus still reads fixtureBytes NOT-AUTHORED on all four, which is correct — that catalog is not edited by this one.

The expected words are quoted, not invented. NT-3's expected reproduces provider-only-output-contract.v3 negativeTests.NT-3.pass verbatim in full. The two EV-2 members quote the first two sentences of NT-5.pass and substitute a class-specific third sentence; the EV-3 member quotes NT-5.pass's third sentence 'No unknown-to-covered conversion.' verbatim. That is lawful specialisation of pinned words, not new law.

The appliesFindingsOf de-duplication is sound. All nine Claude ids (M1-M5, S1-S4) and all five Codex ids (G23FXV1-M1..M5) appear exactly once across the shared and claudeOnly groups, and each shared grouping pairs findings that are genuinely the same class. The idCollisionNote correctly warns that both reviewers used bare M-numbers.

The widening key in the widens fixture is not invented: imports/resolved-target with source and target both sha256:aaaa… is byte-identical to keys[0] of the pinned cross-universe-unavailable-two-targets domain. It is unrequested with respect to the types stage while remaining a fully constructible live key, which is the correct construction for a widening.

cborConstruction.coverageKeyOrder specifies sorting the full CoverageKeyV1 maps rather than any projection, and the authored bytes honour that. This matters because sorting on relation text alone would have produced the opposite order in the widens fixture.

The remeasurementClause is well formed and its own precondition holds: recordedInputs.HEAD equals the top-level head, and file 08, leftover-join v4, occupancy v2, frozen v1 and the four v2 fixtures are all unmoved at review time.

delivery.v2 and fact-plane.v1 are mode 0644 rather than 0444 on disk. The dispatch scopes the freeze-check to the subject, the four authoredCatalog fixtures and frozen v1, all of which are 0444, and both files match their cited digests exactly. Recorded as an observation about repository custody, not as a finding against this subject.

codexCounterpart: docs/coop/artifacts/g23-fixture-corpus.v2.review-independent.codex.json — existed at review time; named by the dispatch and NOT opened. This verdict is independent of it.
decision: REJECT — 1 MUST-FIX, 1 SHOULD-FIX. v2 is a substantial and largely successful repair of v1: twelve of the fourteen v1 findings are landed, and the three commitment constructions, the canonical key ordering, the closed-type conformance and the NT-3 vector copy all survive first-principles recomputation rather than merely being asserted. The corpus applies nothing, invents no schema, no D9 code and no 7.1 recipe, does not SATISFY DR-133, does not open Class A, does not execute G23, and does not close leftover-design of OBL-G23-FX-AUTHORING. It fails on the one property the current occupancy names twice and in both directions: the EV-2 narrows fixture, measured against the very domain vector the subject pins for it, also converts unknown to covered, so EV-2 and EV-3 are collapsed and a retained refusal on EV-2 would be unattributable. The two v1 findings that asked for exact retained baselines are recorded ACCEPTED but are landed for EV-3 alone. The remedy is narrow and mechanical — declare the pinned unknown baseline for both EV-2 members and hold the surviving narrows key at unknown/provider-unavailable so cardinality is the only mutation — and a v3 carrying it should clear.
